_comment: Approved security suppressions. Every '# noqa: S<n>' (flake8-bandit) and '# nosec' (bandit) comment in src/ or hub/ MUST be listed here with a justification, or CI fails (util/check_security_gates.py, run by util/lint.py). Adding an entry requires PR review — this is the gate that would have caught the GAIA hub tar-slip (CWE-22), where a '# noqa: S202 - hub artifacts are trusted' silenced an unvalidated tarfile.extractall. Keyed by (path, rule), not line number. See SECURITY.md.

suppressions.justification: git is a fixed, trusted executable; args are a constructed list, never shell-interpreted
'uv pip install' args are a constructed list (no user string), never shell-interpreted
native binary path is an installed hub artifact (operator-controlled); args are constructed, not shell
binds 0.0.0.0 only on explicit caller opt-in (documented flag), never by default
Running shell commands is this module's purpose. The whitelist and path policy that decide what may run stay in shell_tools.py, and apply per pipeline segment before anything reaches here.

argv is always a constructed list, never shell-interpreted by Python. It names either the generated script this module wrote (which sources a command validated per segment by shell_tools.py) or a skill-granted binary, which is run as argv precisely so its arguments cannot act.
taskkill is a Windows system binary invoked by name with a pid from this module's own child. The alternative is orphaning the process tree a timed-out command started.
